clue.text: Fillet of borogove (a lot of meat)

indicators.note: Fillet of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Jabberwocky borogove, filleted, yields a heap of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'of meat' as the definition, but 'of' only links; 'meat' alone is the noun that stands in for the answer. 'Fillet of' cuts the letters out of 'borogove (a lot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Calf flesh is a kind of butcher's meat, so the meat names it by its general class.

clue.text: Bernini forced to accept 1,000 people's money

indicators.note: to accept means the rearranged name takes in another piece within it
letters that are forced are pushed out of shape, so the sculptor's name is rearranged

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: The baroque sculptor Bernini is made to take on a thousand people's cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' scrambles BERNINI and 'to accept' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chinese currency's name translates literally as 'the people's currency', so the definition is a near-translation.

clue.text: Putting up an objection about colour

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: nay is an old word of refusal or objection
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone raises an objection to a choice of paint colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting up' turns C plus NAY upside down in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenish-blue shade, one of the printer's primary inks, is a colour.

clue.text: All forms of uranium are equals, no question

parts.note: in an equation 'is' stands for equals, as in two and two is four
O, the figure nought, stands for none or no
a topic is a question or matter under discussion

explanation.surface: A physics teacher insists that every form of uranium is equal, no arguing.
explanation.definitionFit: Variants of one element share a place in the periodic table, which is what this adjective describes, so every variety of uranium qualifies.

clue.text: Migrants are found in boat

indicators.note: found in says one word sits inside another

parts.note: a tug is a small powerful boat used for towing

explanation.surface: Refugees are discovered aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests boat people, but the definition points to Saharan desert nomads.
explanation.definitionFit: This Berber people of the Sahara are traditionally nomadic, wandering herders, hence migrants.

clue.text: Juliet, in her ballet-dancing novel

indicators.note: in puts one letter inside the rearranged words
dancing letters move around, so these words are rearranged

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Juliet appears in her ballet, Romeo and Juliet, dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' rearranges HER BALLET and 'in' sets J among the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Sylvia Plath's only novel, published in 1963, has this title.

clue.text: It's sought by one, only ending in ghetto

parts.note: a means one, as in a dog

indicators.note: in puts that letter inside the word for ghetto

parts.note: a ghetto is a run-down district, a slum

indicators.note: ending picks the final letter of the word only

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a place, ending up only in a ghetto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ending' takes Y from 'only' and 'in' places it in SLUM, after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuge or political protection is what a refugee seeks, so it is the thing sought.

clue.text: Boatman in the Guardian, home of slithy toves

indicators.note: in puts the sailor inside the newspaper's pronoun

parts.note: a newspaper speaks of itself as we in its editorials
AB, able-bodied seaman, is a boatman; Boatman is also the setter's name

explanation.surface: The setter Boatman is in the Guardian, as home to Jabberwocky's slithy toves.
explanation.walkthrough: A newspaper refers to itself in the first person plural, so the Guardian gives the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: In Jabberwocky the slithy toves gyre and gimble on this grassy plot, which Humpty Dumpty explains.

clue.text: It's found on board galley: the last two across the sea to France

indicators.note: across says those two letters straddle the French sea, one each side
the last two picks the final pair of letters of the word galley

parts.note: mer is French for sea

explanation.surface: A ship's galley crosses the Channel to France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'across' means the two letters straddle the French word, one on each side.
explanation.definitionFit: The abrasive grit coats a nail file called an emery board, so it is found on a board.

clue.text: Hence cooking us a Thai curry found there

parts.note: so means therefore, hence

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: So, cooking us a Thai curry, you find it's from there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thai' looks like part of the definition but belongs to the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: India and its neighbours are where curry comes from, so the region is where curry is found.

clue.text: One covers nonsense creature's return

indicators.note: return means the joined words are read backwards

parts.note: rot is nonsense, rubbish
an animal is a creature

explanation.surface: One person stands in for a nonsense creature that comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' reverses ROT plus ANIMAL; the apostrophe-s is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A machine that seals documents in plastic film is one that covers them.

clue.text: Gimble freely, no head for mimsy nonsense

indicators.note: freely means the letters are rearranged at will
no means the letter is taken away
head for picks the first letter of the word mimsy

explanation.surface: Gimble and mimsy, both Jabberwocky words, are used freely as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no head for mimsy' drops M from GIMBLE, and 'freely' rearranges GIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Bilge is slang for worthless talk, like the foul water in a ship's hull.

clue.text: One point after another, leading, relentless

parts.note: N, north, is one point of the compass
on can mean after, as in following on
S, south, is another compass point
top means leading, first

explanation.surface: Scoring one point after another keeps a side ahead, relentlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that never pauses is without stops, i.e. unceasing.

clue.text: Nonsense creature's tail is, of course, short

indicators.note: tail keeps only the end of the creature's name, its back portion

parts.note: the frumious Bandersnatch is a creature in Lewis Carroll's Jabberwocky

explanation.surface: A nonsense creature's tail is short, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' keeps only the last five letters of BANDERSNATCH, dropping BANDERS.
explanation.definitionFit: This is slang shortening of naturally, meaning of course.

clue.text: With thanks, able to be part of Europe

indicators.note: to be suggests the letters can be made into something new, a rearrangement

explanation.surface: With thanks, someone becomes able to join Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be' is the anagram signal on THANKS ABLE; 'With' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The peninsula of south-east Europe, including Serbia, Bulgaria and Greece, is a region of Europe.

clue.text: Laugh madly about, say, Boris Johnson's capacity to caper clumsily

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round another piece
madly means the letters are rearranged wildly

parts.note: Boris Johnson sat as an MP, Member of Parliament, an example of that capacity

explanation.surface: People laugh at Boris Johnson's clumsy capering.
explanation.walkthrough: The verb was coined by Lewis Carroll in Jabberwocky, fitting the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: To move in a heavy, ungainly, bounding way is to caper clumsily.

clue.text: Callooh! Callay! Both at last within reach

indicators.note: the clue word that signals this step
at last picks the final letter of each of the two exclamations

parts.note: both is used with and, as in both this and that

explanation.surface: Jabberwocky's cry of joy, both shouts at last reaching their goal.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letters of 'Callooh!' and 'Callay!' are joined by AND: H and Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Something close at hand is convenient, near enough to reach.

clue.text: Nonsense creature's paunch on the table

definitions.meaning: the stomach lining of a cow or sheep, cooked and served as food

explanation.definitionFit: Ox stomach is a cheap dish, and the word also means worthless rubbish talk.

clue.text: Boatman's people, say, could be grand

indicators.note: say means the word sounds like another when spoken

parts.note: a boatman's people are his crew, the sailors who work the boat

explanation.surface: The setter Boatman's crew think things could be grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' gives the sound of CREW. Grand cru is a top rank of French vineyard or wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine classification or growth, with grand cru the highest, so grand is one kind.

clue.text: Clumsy creature raised largely without master

indicators.note: in a down clue raised means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a gnu is an African antelope, a creature

indicators.note: without means the letter for master is taken out

parts.note: mainly means largely, for the most part
M is short for master, as in MA

explanation.surface: A clumsy creature brought up largely without a master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' reverses GNU and 'without master' takes M from MAINLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking grace in movement is a near synonym of clumsy.

clue.text: Origin of teriyaki: Jabberwock's head with a Chinese way to cook its rump, say?

indicators.note: head picks the first letter of the monster's name

parts.words: Chinese way to cook its rump, say?
parts.note: the rump of Jabberwock is wock, sounding like wok, the Chinese cooking pan

explanation.surface: A Jabberwock cooked Chinese-style in a wok yields a teriyaki dish.
explanation.walkthrough: A wok is a kind of pan, and the end of Jabberwock sounds like it, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Teriyaki glazing is a Japanese cooking style, so the country is where it originated.

clue.text: Notices unfinished programme on comics

indicators.note: unfinished means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a plan is a programme of action
cards are comical people, jokers

explanation.surface: Someone notices an unfinished TV programme on comedians.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' means placed above, so the first piece sits on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Posters or signs displayed publicly are notices.

clue.text: Nonsense creature was hunted at first

parts.note: a hog is a pig, a creature

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of hunted

explanation.surface: A nonsense creature was hunted at first, like Carroll's Snark.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigswill is the literal sense, used figuratively for worthless talk.

clue.text: Force weapon to turn aside

parts.note: g is the symbol for the force of gravity
a lance is a long spear, a weapon

explanation.surface: A force uses a weapon to make an enemy turn aside.
explanation.definitionFit: A blow that strikes obliquely and is deflected is said to turn aside.

clue.text: Nonsense creature's behind rank odour

indicators.note: behind puts the creature after the smell

parts.note: hum is British slang for a bad smell
a bug is an insect, a creature

explanation.surface: A nonsense creature's backside gives off a rank odour.
explanation.walkthrough: HUM is everyday British slang for a stink.
explanation.definitionFit: Deceptive talk or sham is an old synonym for nonsense, famous from Scrooge.

clue.text: Gyre madly about island country

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round another piece
madly means the letters are rearranged wildly

parts.note: the Isle of Man is an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: Gyre, from Jabberwocky, whirls wildly around an island country.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man is a self-governing island between Britain and Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: The central European state is a country.

clue.text: Nonsense creature's rank order

indicators.note: order means the letters are sorted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A nonsense creature's rank in the order of things.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s supplies S, and 'order' rearranges S RANK.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark is a nonsense poem about this imaginary beast.

clue.text: Trauma at the heart of Jabberwock's creator

indicators.note: at the heart of keeps only the central letters, dropping both ends

parts.note: Lewis Carroll wrote the poem Jabberwocky

explanation.surface: A trauma lies at the core of the poet behind the Jabberwock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the heart of' keeps the central four letters of LEWIS CARROLL, removing LEWI and ROLL.
explanation.definitionFit: A lasting mark of injury, physical or emotional, can stand for a trauma.

clue.text: At sea, couple with rum to drink, when spliced

definitions.text: with rum to drink, when spliced

parts.note: the main is an old word for the open sea
a brace is a pair or couple, as of pheasants

explanation.surface: Sailors couple up at sea, with rum to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Splice the mainbrace' was the Royal Navy order to issue an extra tot of rum.
explanation.definitionFit: The naval phrase to splice the mainbrace means to serve out drink, so the rope is the rum one when spliced.

clue.text: Nonsense creature

definitions.meaning: an adult male bovine, a beast

explanation.definitionFit: Slang for rubbish talk and the male of cattle share this one spelling.

clue.text: It's always found in nonsense verse

indicators.note: found in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: It is always to be found in nonsense poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means at all times, as in forever, a synonym of always.

clue.text: About a nurse, overcome by real stress showing

indicators.note: overcome by means the pieces are covered, held inside the word for real

parts.note: actual means real
C is short for circa, Latin for about
EN is an enrolled nurse

explanation.surface: A nurse is overcome by stress that really shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' is the definition here, in the sense of metrical emphasis, not anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes rhythm based on accents, so it means marked by stress.

clue.text: Society licenses odd doings, generating eyewash of the first order

indicators.note: of the first order points to the first letter of each of the words

explanation.surface: A society permits odd activities that produce first-rate eyewash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the first order' takes the initials of licenses, odd, doings, generating, eyewash.
explanation.definitionFit: A Masonic branch or similar fraternal group is a society.
